newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND SAYS EU STABILITY PACT NOT LEGALLY BINDING.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND SAYS EU STABILITY PACT NOT LEGALLY BINDING.

text.p: The Finnish parliament's constitutional committee said on Thursday a potential budget stability pact between European Union leaders would not be legally binding, but carry significant weight politically.
The committee is Finland's highest authority on legislative interpretation and its rulings cannot be appealed.

"Formally speaking, the stability programme is not legally binding and would thus not restrict parliament's independent decision-making powers in its annual work on the (national) budget," the constitutional committee said in a statement.

The stability pact would "in fact carry significant weight and the political possibilities to diverge from the programme approved by the Council of Ministers or from the Council's recommendations cannot be regarded as great," it added.
If Finland joined monetary union, the stability pact would become a significant document affecting Finnish medium-term monetary policy and annual national budgets, the committee said.
European Union leaders are due to attend a summit in Dublin this weekend and the budget stability pact is the item on the agenda most closely monitored by financial markets.
